finding.claim: The purge handler calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards the boolean result, so the admin check is never enforced. Any authenticated user can run purgeAll().
finding.source: Any authenticated HTTP user without the admin permission who sends a request to the purge endpoint
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a destructive admin-only operation

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) gets the requesting user, who may lack admin
checkPerm returns false for a non-admin but the return value is ignored as a bare statement

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm has no side effects and does not write a 403 or abort. There is no other check in the handler. The sibling rotateKeys correctly uses mustPerm and returns on false. Middleware is not visible in this directory, and nothing in the file shows it enforcing admin on this route.

verdict.guard_found: checkPerm (handlers.go:12) returns a bool with no side effects, and its result is discarded at line 26. No other check exists in the handler. No routing or middleware code is present in the directory.
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm as a bare statement and discards the bool, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any authenticated user, unlike rotateKeys at handlers.go:33 which tests mustPerm and returns on false.
